# gitmoap_repository_import (Data Source)

Get a repository's import. The import that created this repository: where it comes from, where it stands, how far it has got, and what it did not bring as it was. Anyone who can see the repository may read it.

The token needs `import:read`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "gitmoap_repository_by_path" "api" {
  full_path = "acme/platform/api"
}

data "gitmoap_repository_import" "api" {
  repo_id = data.gitmoap_repository_by_path.api.repository_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `repo_id` (String) Repository ID

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When it was started.
- `error` (String) Why it failed, when it did.
- `finished_at` (String) When it ended.
- `full_path` (String) The repository's path.
- `import_id` (String) Identifies an import of a repository from another host.
- `progress` (Attributes) How many of each kind an import has brought so far. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--progress))
- `report` (Attributes) What an import did not bring as it was. A review's comments arrive as comments; a review's approval never arrives, since an approval here is given here. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--report))
- `repository_id` (String)
- `requested_by` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--requested_by))
- `resume_after` (String) While a source's rate limit holds it, when it carries on.
- `source` (String) Where an import comes from: `git` is any HTTPS git host and brings history only; `github`, `gitlab` and `bitbucket` also bring work items, merge requests, comments, labels, milestones and releases.
- `source_url` (String) The source's address, as given. A token is never part of it.
- `state` (String) Where an import stands: `queued` before its worker starts, `fetching` while the history arrives, `importing_metadata` while work items, merge requests and the rest arrive, then `done`, `failed` or `cancelled`.

<a id="nestedatt--progress"></a>
### Nested Schema for `progress`

Read-Only:

- `comments` (Number) Comments brought.
- `labels` (Number) Labels brought.
- `merge_requests` (Number) Merge requests brought.
- `milestones` (Number) Milestones brought.
- `releases` (Number) Releases brought.
- `work_items` (Number) Work items brought.


<a id="nestedatt--report"></a>
### Nested Schema for `report`

Read-Only:

- `assignees_not_kept` (Number) Assignees on the source who were not kept: nobody here is linked to them, the person they
are linked to cannot read the repository, the work item already had five, or they were on a
merge request, which has reviewers here rather than assignees.
- `reviews_not_counted` (Number) Review comments on the source's merge requests, brought as comments. None of them, and no
approval on the source, counts toward a merge request's approvals here.
- `skipped` (Attributes List) The items, at most two hundred. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--report--skipped))
- `skipped_not_listed` (Number) How many more were skipped than are listed.

<a id="nestedatt--report--skipped"></a>
### Nested Schema for `report.skipped`

Read-Only:

- `kind` (String) A kind of thing an import brings: a label, a milestone, a work item, a merge request, a comment or a release.
- `reason` (String) What happened to it, in a sentence.
- `source_id` (String) Its id on the source.



<a id="nestedatt--requested_by"></a>
### Nested Schema for `requested_by`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor, and empty on a redacted one and on an outside author.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor and on an outside author (`imported`).
- `imported` (Attributes) An author who wrote on another host — a work item, a merge request, a comment, a release an import
brought — and whom nobody here is linked to yet. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--requested_by--imported))
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.

<a id="nestedatt--requested_by--imported"></a>
### Nested Schema for `requested_by.imported`

Read-Only:

- `identity_id` (String) The outside author's id among the organization's imported identities.
- `login` (String) Their login on that host.
- `name` (String) Their name on that host, when it gave one.
- `profile_url` (String) Their profile's address on that host, when it gave one.
- `source_host` (String) The host they wrote on, such as `github.com`.
